newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bank sector to see further concentration.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bank sector to see further concentration.

text.p: The Belgian banking sector saw further mergers in the first few months of 1997 and indications are the trend towards concentration is not over yet, the sector's watchdog the Banking and Finance Commission (CBF) said.

Notable takeovers in the first half included Cera's buy of Indosuez Belgium and Bacob's purchase of Paribas Belgium, chairman Jean-Louis Duplat of the CBF told a news conference on 1996 and early 1997 trends on Monday.
Both Cera and Bacob are top seven Belgian banks.
At the end of the first half there were 135 credit institutions in Belgium, down from 141 at the end of 1996 and 144 at the end of 1995.

In 1996 the number of Belgian credit institutions fell by three despite the conversion of three former brokerages into banks. The number of subsidiaries of Japanese banks decreased by three as well, the number of French bank subsidiaries by two.
The CBF said that on the whole smaller institutions, with a balance sheet total of less than 10 billion Belgian francs, were affected.
The merger trend reached unprecedented levels in the brokerage sector, affecting over a quarter of all companies. Their number fell to 62 at the end of 1996 from 85 at end-1995.
"It was a spectacular fall," Duplat said, noting there had been 124 brokerages in 1991.
The contraction slowed in 1997. From a total of 84 companies working in the investment sector as a whole at the end of last year there were 79 left at the end of June 1997.
The sector includes capital management companies and subsidiaries of foreign investment companies.
Duplat said the mergers mainly affected privately or family-owned companies. Their number fell to 48 at end-1996 from 69 at the end of 1995.

The balance sheet total of companies in the investment sector fell to 74.9 billion Belgian francs from 84.7 billion francs. In the brokerage sector however, turnover grew to 7.77 billion francs and net profit to 1.72 billion from 6.57 billion and 1.11 billion respectively.
